rejected_claims.title: IncomePerMinute estimator assumes gradual debit but the sim debits full cost up front; value is an unsmoothed per-interval spike
rejected_claims.claim_evidence: 6c59705: income is now the credit delta over FeatureOptions.IncomeWindowSeconds (15 s) plus the modelled spend integrated over the same window, and the doc comment now describes the sim's up-front debit. Test: IncomePerMinute_IsWindowed_SoAnUpFrontDebitIsNotAMultiThousandSpike (15 fps, 900-credit tank debited up front) failed before with worst |income| 804600/min and passes after with at most 3600/min.
skeptics:
The fix works in steady state but leaves the finding's own scenario open. On HEAD (8e92463), src/Bindery.Ra2.Bot/Features/FeatureCompiler.Economy.cs:79-100 (WindowedIncomePerSecond) is a real 15 s window: credit delta plus integrated spend, divided by `span`. The doc comment now describes the up-front debit correctly. The named test IncomePerMinute_IsWindowed_SoAnUpFrontDebitIsNotAMultiThousandSpike (tests/Bindery.Ra2.Bot.Tests/Features/FeatureCompilerReviewTests.cs:98) does exercise the old defect. Under the old one-frame formula, the enqueue frame gives (-900 / (1/15) + 90) * 60 = -804600/min, which matches the claim.

The gap is the start of the match. The window is not padded: when history is younger than IncomeWindowSeconds, `baseline = history[0]` and `span = now - t0` is shorter than 15 s. Nothing rescales it or holds income at zero while the window fills. The test only debits at t=20, after the window is full, so it never reaches this case.

In a scratch copy (git archive to scratchpad/sk1-income, run through the same test harness) I wrote the named test again with the tank queued at t=2 instead of t=20. It FAILS on HEAD with `worst |income| 27000/min`, against the 3600 bound. The original test passes in the same run.

Queued at t=1, which is the finding's failure_scenario of "900-credit tank queued at t=0 at 1 s cadence", the estimate is about -54000/min, the same size the finding reported. Harvester dumps and enqueues in the first 15 s spike the same way. Bots enqueue at match start, so IncomePerMinute conditions, BudgetLedger.BeginPeriod (BotRuntime.cs:237), FeatureVector and the "income <= 0" gate in OperationalPlanner.cs:122 still see single-frame swings in the opening seconds. The defect is reduced to the first IncomeWindowSeconds, not gone, and the test does not cover that window.

Git status of /projects/dev/_wt/bindery-ra2-bot is clean.

The fix works once 15 s of history exists, but the spike still happens early in every game. On HEAD 8e92463 (which includes 6c59705), WindowedIncomePerSecond (src/Bindery.Ra2.Bot/Features/FeatureCompiler.Economy.cs:79-100) uses the oldest sample, history[0], as the baseline whenever the history covers less than IncomeWindowSeconds, and divides by the actual span: `span = now.SecondsSince(baseline.Time)` and `return (credits - baseline.Credits + spent) / span`. For the first 15 s of a game the divisor is not 15 s but the elapsed time, down to one frame. So an up-front debit in the opening seconds, when the bot starts its build order, still gives the one-interval spike described in the finding. The named test IncomePerMinute_IsWindowed_SoAnUpFrontDebitIsNotAMultiThousandSpike does not exercise this: it enqueues the tank at t=20 s, after the window has filled.

Reproduction: in a scratch copy made with git archive (/tmp/claude-1000/-projects-dev/78fca569-75ab-48b7-89eb-b3f8e360e1c0/scratchpad/inc2), I added a copy of the named test that enqueues the same 900-credit, 10 s tank at t=1 s instead of t=20 s. It fails with "worst |income| 54000/min", which is exactly the -54000/min enqueue spike in the original failure_scenario. The committed test passes in the same run. The phantom positive income is capped at 3600/min in that case. At 15 fps, an enqueue on the second frame would give roughly -810000/min, by the same formula.

The worktree git status is clean.

rejected_claims.title: IncomePerMinute is a one-frame derivative and produces multi-million spikes
rejected_claims.claim_evidence: Same root cause as the sim up-front debit finding. Fixed in 6c59705 and covered by IncomePerMinute_IsWindowed_SoAnUpFrontDebitIsNotAMultiThousandSpike (804600/min before the fix, at most 3600/min after).
skeptics:
The fix only works once the window has filled, so the spike still happens early in every game. HEAD is 8e92463, which includes 6c59705.

**Where it breaks.** WindowedIncomePerSecond is in src/Bindery.Ra2.Bot/Features/FeatureCompiler.Economy.cs:79-100. When no history sample is at or before the cutoff (now - 15 s), it falls back to history[0] and divides by span = now - history[0].Time. For the first 15 s of a game (and after any history gap) that span can be one frame, 1/15 s. An enqueue in that period is debited up front, and the previous sample had no spending modelled. The estimator is then the same one-frame derivative the finding describes. The early game is when build orders queue their first items.

**Reproduction.** I added a test to a scratch copy (git archive HEAD into scratchpad/skep2-income; the worktree is untouched and git status is clean). It uses the same setup as the named test, except the 900-credit / 10 s tank is queued at t = 1/15 s instead of t = 20 s. Result: `worst |income| 810000/min`, against the claimed bound of 3600. The named test IncomePerMinute_IsWindowed_SoAnUpFrontDebitIsNotAMultiThousandSpike passes, but only because it holds credits flat for 20 s. That fills the 15 s window before the debit, so it never exercises the early-game failure.

**Conclusion.** The windowing does bound the steady-state error. But the failure scenario (a multi-hundred-thousand-per-minute spike on an enqueue frame that feeds conditions, FeatureVector, the prompt and the ledger) still occurs on HEAD. It is the same order of magnitude as the original 804600/min. Possible fixes: require span >= IncomeWindowSeconds (or return 0 or a flat value until then), or divide by the full window instead of the partial span.

The claim that this is fixed does not hold. Commit 6c59705 only partly fixed the defect: an enqueue before 15 s of history exists still produces a spike of hundreds of thousands per minute.

On HEAD 8e92463, `WindowedIncomePerSecond` in /projects/dev/_wt/bindery-ra2-bot/src/Bindery.Ra2.Bot/Features/FeatureCompiler.Economy.cs (lines ~79-97) falls back to `history[0]` when no sample is at or before the cutoff. It then divides by `span = now - baseline.Time`, and early in the game that span can be a fraction of a second, not the 15 s window. The window bound only holds once 15 s of history exist.

Reproduction: a scratch copy (git archive to scratchpad/sk1-income, nothing changed in the worktree) with one added test. It is identical to the named test except the 900-credit / 10 s tank is enqueued at t=0.2 s instead of t=20 s. Result: `SKEPTIC worst |income| 270000/min`. The named test passed in the same run, and 270000/min is 75x its 3600/min bound. That is the original failure scenario, a huge negative income on the frame the simulator debits the full cost, and bot openings enqueue production in the first seconds.

The named test `IncomePerMinute_IsWindowed_SoAnUpFrontDebitIsNotAMultiThousandSpike` enqueues only at t=20 s, after the window is full, so it never exercises the warm-up case.

Two other parts of the finding also remain:
- Samples are still pushed on every compile, not once per second (`FeatureCompiler.PushSample`).
- The 5/15/60 s income trend deltas still compare against a single stored sample (`FeatureCompiler.Baseline`).

Git status in the worktree is clean (0 entries).

rejected_claims.title: Decision-log content, and the LLM prompt, depend on the process culture, so hashes differ between machines and locales
rejected_claims.claim_evidence: Commit 976521e ('format decision rationales and reasons in the invariant culture'). ContextualBanditStrategist.cs:63 and :91, DistilledStrategist, PinnedPlaybookStrategist, PlaybookSelector and StrategyRationale.Explain all use string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, ...). FeatureCompiler.Events and the planner notes were changed in the same commit. The Arena and Tune csproj set InvariantGlobalization=true. Test RationaleTests.Rationales_do_not_depend_on_the_machine_locale compares every strategist's rationale under de-DE and the invariant culture. Outside this area, IntentValidator.cs lines 56, 63, 78, 166, 169 and 203 still interpolate doubles in the current culture (see cross_area).
skeptics:
The defect is only partly fixed on HEAD 8e92463, so "already_fixed" does not hold. The strategist rationales are now culture-invariant: StrategyRationale.Explain and the others wrap their text in string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, ...). However, the original finding also names the IntentValidator messages as part of this defect ("validator messages in IntentValidator.cs ... written into validation records"), and those still depend on the culture.

1. src/Bindery.Ra2.Bot/Arbitration/IntentValidator.cs still uses current-culture double interpolation at lines 56, 63, 78, 166, 169 and 203. Examples: $"Proposal is {age:0.###} s old ...", $"Budget shares summed to {sum:0.####}; normalised to 1."
2. Those messages go into the decision log. src/Bindery.Ra2.Bot/Runtime/StrategyScheduler.cs:457 and :511 write a DecisionRecordKinds.Validation record whose issues array is built by Issues() (line 523-524), and that array includes message = i.Message. So under fi-FI or de-DE, a proposal that triggers an ExpiryTooLong or BudgetSum warning, or a stale reject, logs "1,02" where en-US logs "1.02", and the log hash differs. That breaks the "equal on every machine and locale" contract in DecisionLog.cs.
3. InvariantGlobalization=true is set only in tools/Bindery.Ra2.Bot.Arena and tools/Bindery.Ra2.Bot.Tune. There is nothing in Directory.Build.props and no CA1305 rule. So the Bot library is not protected when another host runs it, such as src/Bindery.Ra2.Adapter/Bot/Ra2BotHost.cs, which drives BotRuntime, or the test process.

The claim itself concedes these IntentValidator lines remain and calls them "outside this area". They are, however, inside this finding's own scope and failure scenario (decision-log content that depends on culture). Git status is clean (0 changes).

The claim holds only in part. The defect is still present on HEAD 8e92463 wherever the bot library runs without InvariantGlobalization.

What is fixed:
- Commit 976521e wraps the strategist rationales (ContextualBanditStrategist, DistilledStrategist, PinnedPlaybookStrategist, PlaybookSelector, StrategyRationale.Explain), FeatureCompiler.Events and some planner notes in string.Create(InvariantCulture, ...).
- The Arena and Tune csproj files set InvariantGlobalization=true.
- The claim's cross_area note is wrong. IntentValidator lines 56, 63, 78, 166, 169 and 203 are already invariant: Reject and Warn (IntentValidator.cs:343-347) take a FormattableString and apply FormattableString.Invariant, and have done so since 2b6aafd.

What is still broken:
- src/Bindery.Ra2.Bot/Operations/OperationalPlanner.cs:225 builds `Queue(power, $"power-first: {rule.TypeId} needs {-rule.Power} but surplus is {belief.Power.Surplus}")` in the current culture. Power.Surplus is an int (World.cs:128, Produced - Drained) and is negative whenever the base is in low power.
- These notes reach the hashed decision log through BotRuntime.cs:302 (`notes = plan.Notes`).
- I checked this with a scratch net8 program under nix dotnet-sdk_8. An int of -150 formats as "-150" under en-US but as "−150" (U+2212, 6 UTF-8 bytes instead of 4) under fi-FI, sv-SE and nb-NO. So a log recorded in a Finnish, Swedish or Norwegian locale hashes differently. That is the failure_scenario, and it breaks DecisionLog's promise that equal logs hash equal on every machine and locale.

Why InvariantGlobalization does not cover it:
- It is set only on Arena and Tune.
- The library itself is not invariant. Neither Bindery.Ra2.Bot nor Bindery.Ra2.Adapter sets it, and Directory.Build.props has no InvariantGlobalization or CA1305.
- The live host src/Bindery.Ra2.Adapter/Bot/Ra2BotHost.cs, which drives BotRuntime, runs in whatever culture its process has.

What the test covers:
- RationaleTests.Rationales_do_not_depend_on_the_machine_locale checks only strategist rationales under de-DE.
- de-DE uses an ASCII minus, so it would not catch this. It also does not exercise planner notes.

Other lines I looked at use non-negative ints (credits, costs) or enums.

Git status is clean. The scratch program lives only in the scratchpad (scratchpad/cult).

rejected_claims.title: TwoSpeedStrategist sends event-driven and replan requests to the fast (Refine) strategist when the event arrived while a request was in flight
rejected_claims.claim_evidence: Commit 15d15fb, src/Bindery.Ra2.Bot/Strategy/TwoSpeedStrategist.cs. Each request is now settled against the next context's ActiveIntent. The fast strategist is used only while the active intent is the slow strategist's own choice or a refinement of it. A slow turn counts only when its answer was applied, or was delivered while that commitment stood. Test StrategyLifecycleTests.Two_speed_sends_the_request_an_event_deferred_to_the_slow_strategist uses the real scheduler, validator and arbiter: the event arrives at t=2, the slow answer is late-discarded at t=3, and the deferred request must go to slow. Before the fix it failed with 'Expected: 2 Actual: 1' slow calls; after the fix it passes. One case remains: the slow strategist's own intent is active, an event late-discards its newer answer, and the deferred request has no event in its features. This class cannot tell that from an arbiter refusal, and replan:* reasons are not visible to it either. That case needs the trigger in StrategistContext (see cross_area).
skeptics:
The HEAD code routing looks correct. src/Bindery.Ra2.Bot/Strategy/TwoSpeedStrategist.cs sends a request to the slow strategist whenever the trigger is event:* or replan:*, whenever the active intent is not owned, and whenever the fallback's features show a new event. So I found no live failure. The claim still fails, because the evidence does not support it on HEAD (8e92463).

1. The named test changed after 15d15fb. Commit f4dc0ee ("two-speed event test expects the in-flight request superseded") came after 30b307c, where the scheduler began superseding unusable in-flight requests immediately. In tests/Bindery.Ra2.Bot.Tests/Strategy/StrategyLifecycleTests.cs, Two_speed_sends_the_request_an_event_deferred_to_the_slow_strategist now asserts that the in-flight request is ProposalFailed at t=2 and that LateDiscarded is empty. The claim describes a late-discard at t=3, so the scenario it cites no longer exists.

2. Mutation check. I ran it in a scratch copy made with git archive HEAD, which is now deleted, and the worktree git status is clean. I replaced TwoSpeedStrategist.cs with its pre-fix version (15d15fb^) and ran StrategyLifecycleTests. The named test PASSED with the fix reverted: at t=2 the event is in that frame's features, so the old newEvent check already sends the request to the slow strategist. Only Two_speed_never_lets_the_fast_strategist_renew_a_placeholder_after_a_failed_slow_request failed, where fast got ActiveIntent fb-0. That test covers the placeholder or failed-slow finding, not the event-deferred one. Result: 1 failed, 4 passed.

So the named test no longer exercises the event-deferred routing defect. Nothing in the cited evidence shows the Trigger-based routing is needed or tested. The self-reported remaining case (own intent active, event late-discards the answer, no event in the features) depends on Trigger, and no test covers it.

The defect looks absent on HEAD 8e92463, but the named test does not exercise it, so the evidence does not support the claim as written.

1. The code fix is present. In /projects/dev/_wt/bindery-ra2-bot/src/Bindery.Ra2.Bot/Strategy/TwoSpeedStrategist.cs, Settle() checks each request against the next context's ActiveIntent and tracks the owned intent. The later commit 8e92463 also added routing on StrategistContext.Trigger: every event:* and replan:* request goes to the slow strategist. That closes the "one case remains" gap the claim called open, so the claim's description is out of date.

2. The named test has changed and no longer catches the defect. Commits 30b307c ("scheduler supersedes unusable requests") and f4dc0ee ("two-speed event test expects the in-flight request superseded") changed Two_speed_sends_the_request_an_event_deferred_to_the_slow_strategist. The claim describes it as "late-discarded at t=3". On HEAD the test asserts `Assert.Empty(log.OfKind(DecisionRecordKinds.LateDiscarded))`: the in-flight request is superseded at t=2 and the new request starts on the same frame, and that frame's features show the event.
   - Mutation check: I put the pre-fix TwoSpeedStrategist (15d15fb^) into a scratch copy of HEAD and ran the StrategyLifecycleTests.
   - The named test passed. Only Two_speed_never_lets_the_fast_strategist_renew_a_placeholder_after_a_failed_slow_request failed (1 failed, 4 passed).
   - So the claimed "Expected: 2 Actual: 1 before the fix" does not reproduce on HEAD. The pre-fix code's feature-based check (an event newer than the previous request) already sends that request to the slow strategist.

3. The deferred-request case is covered by a different test. In a second scratch mutation I kept HEAD's code but turned off the Trigger routing. The full bot suite then had 1 failure out of 742: StrategistContextTests.Two_speed_sends_an_event_triggered_request_to_the_slow_strategist_even_when_its_features_show_no_event. rejected_claims.title: Base-threat override is level-triggered: every proposal during a sustained threat bypasses commitment and posture hysteresis
rejected_claims.claim_evidence: Commit 43bcd0e. IntentArbiter now allows one base-threat override per threat episode. A baseThreatAnswered flag is set when an intent is activated while the threat holds, and cleared in Update once the threat stops. The override also never replaces a Defend or Turtle incumbent. Tests IntentArbiterTests.Base_threat_overrides_commitment_once_per_threat_episode and Base_threat_override_does_not_replace_a_defensive_incumbent failed before the fix and pass after.
skeptics:
The code fix is present and correct on HEAD 8e92463 (43bcd0e is an ancestor). In src/Bindery.Ra2.Bot/Arbitration/IntentArbiter.cs, Update() clears baseThreatAnswered at line 150 when the threat is not holding. Activate() sets it at lines 296-298 when an intent is installed while the threat holds. The override guard at lines 259-261 requires !baseThreatAnswered and a non-Defend/Turtle incumbent. By reading the code, the original Defend/Boom alternation cannot happen on HEAD.

The test evidence does not hold up. Base_threat_overrides_commitment_once_per_threat_episode does not exercise the once-per-episode flag. Its override installs d1, which is generic-defend with Defend posture. Every later wavering proposal is then blocked by the Defend/Turtle-incumbent guard alone, whatever the flag says.

Mutation check in a scratch copy made with git archive (the worktree was never touched): I disabled the flag by changing line 259 to `if ((baseThreatAnswered || true)`. `dotnet test tests/Bindery.Ra2.Bot.Tests -c Release` printed "Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: 741, Skipped: 1". So no test covers the per-episode mechanism the evidence names.

Only the flag fixes the path the finding's verification calls still reachable: an override installs a non-defensive plan, such as Harass or a custom-abort Boom, and the strategist then keeps wavering between non-defensive plans under a sustained threat. That path is untested, so the flag could be removed with every test still passing.

The Defend/Turtle guard is covered: Base_threat_override_does_not_replace_a_defensive_incumbent would fail without it. The fix itself is right, but the claim that the named once-per-episode test failed before the fix and verifies the per-episode behaviour is not supported: it fails only because the Defend guard was missing. Scratch copy removed; git status is clean.

The runtime fix is present on HEAD (8e92463, which contains 43bcd0e). In src/Bindery.Ra2.Bot/Arbitration/IntentArbiter.cs, Decide at lines 259-264 gates the override on `!baseThreatAnswered && incumbent.Posture is not (Defend or Turtle)`. Activate sets `baseThreatAnswered = baseThreatFiring` (line 298), and Update clears the flag when the threat stops (line 150). The finding's exact scenario (generic-defend and allied-boom alternating) is now blocked.

The evidence overstates what the tests show, though. The claim says the named test Base_threat_overrides_commitment_once_per_threat_episode covers the once-per-episode mechanism. Mutation check: I made a scratch copy via git archive at /tmp/claude-1000/-projects-dev/78fca569-75ab-48b7-89eb-b3f8e360e1c0/scratchpad/mut-bt and removed only the `!baseThreatAnswered &&` guard. Test BotRuntimeTests.Ledger_capacity_excludes_what_queued_production_still_owes(true, 335) failed without the BotRuntime change and passes with it; the (false, 1010) case passes both ways. 1. BotRuntime.cs:236-237 now calls `BeginPeriod(now, belief.Credits - unpaid, ...)`, with unpaid = ProductionDebt.Unpaid(rules, belief.Queues). That is a sum over the observed queue items.

Its comment reads "v1 telemetry reports no production queues". Ra2BotTelemetryContract.cs:~67 says "No production-queue event is mapped, so every frame has QueuesKnown false."

With 2000 credits the bot queues a 2000 war factory. The next pass reads about 1950 credits and gets capacity of about 1950 with spent reset. The planner's busyWhileUnreported (OperationalPlanner.cs:142/182) only marks the queue it ordered on as busy, so the vehicle queue then gets a 900 tank and the infantry queue a 200 unit. However, the folding runs on arbiter.History, which is still trimmed to HistoryCapacity=32 raw entries. Every renewal still appends a raw entry: IntentArbiter.cs:337-341 (Renew calls CloseHistory "renewed" plus AddHistory), and AddHistory at 400-405 trims by raw count with no merging. No caller overrides HistoryCapacity, and StrategyScheduler.cs:232 passes arbiter.History unchanged.

On llm+fast (BotAgentFactory.cs:250, StrategicCadenceSeconds=5), after about 32 renewals (~160 s of a steady plan) the earlier switch or abort is evicted before the prompt builder ever sees it. That is the same defect with a longer fuse.

I checked this in a scratch copy of HEAD (since deleted; worktree git status is clean). The probe used the real IntentArbiter and followed the named test: allied-harass at t=0, a switch to allied-boom at t=50, then 36 renewals every 5 s. The prompt history was ["allied-boom"] only, where ["allied-harass","allied-boom"] was expected. The allied-harass "replaced:switch" entry was gone.

The surviving item was also wrong: acceptedAtSeconds=75 instead of 50, with renewals=31, because the start of the chain had been trimmed. The prompt's "History lists one item per plan" is therefore not true beyond the 32-entry window.

The named test uses only 12 renewals, which fit under the 32 cap, so it never exercises this path.

not_fixed.title: RA2 bridge invents empty production queues and zero credits/power instead of reporting them missing
not_fixed.evidence: Still present at HEAD: BuildFrame passes Queues=[] and credits 0 / PowerState(0,0) until the first sample. The root fix needs the Bot contract ObservationFrame to express unknown queues, credits and power, and the OperationalPlanner to suppress queue-driven production when queues are unknown. Both are outside the bridge-ci area; see cross_area. Recording these as MissingFields entries per frame would conflict with the per-payload audit semantics that existing tests pin, so no partial adapter change was made.

not_fixed.title: Every non-self owner is an enemy: neutral, civilian or allied entities become enemy contacts, contest our base and create a base threat
not_fixed.evidence: Still present at b2cbb62: BeliefModel.UpdateEnemyContacts treats every Owner != frame.Self as an enemy. The fix needs a contract change outside this area. Belief cannot tell enemies from neutral or allied houses, because ObservationFrame and ObservedEntity carry no allegiance data. See cross_area for the exact changes.

not_fixed.title: Prompt says a fallback- or emergency-installed intent is committed, though the arbiter yields it to any primary proposal
not_fixed.evidence: The prompt cannot know the arbiter's ActiveRole. StrategistContext does not carry it, and IntentHistoryEntry/Source cannot tell a placeholder apart reliably: in llm-shadow and distilled arms, Selector or Distilled sources are primary. This needs a contract change (see cross_area). Commit 5c495cf closes part of the harm: Refine can no longer promote a placeholder.

not_fixed.title: Inference cost omits cache-creation tokens and every failed request's tokens
not_fixed.evidence: Root cause is outside this area. ProposalCost (src/Bindery.Ra2.Bot/Contracts/Strategy.cs) has no CacheCreationTokens field, and BotArenaAgent (tools) does not sum ProposalFailed costs. The Claude side is ready: ModelUsage carries CacheCreationTokens, and since 0977f7f PriceTable.CostUsd prices creation tokens at 1.25x. The exact changes are in cross_area.
